note: Issue 4666's reported symptom IS a diagnostic, so the predicate quotes the exact wording from the issue body rather than testing for 'an error happened'. Matching any error, or any nonzero exit, would score every release that never supported sampler-array parameters as a textbook reproduction -- and dxc returns E_FAIL (0x80004005) for ordinary diagnosed errors, so exit status says nothing here either. The only tolerance is \s* between the type name and the extent, in case an older release's type printer spaces it differently; the release captures show every probed release in fact prints 'SamplerState [2]' exactly. classify()'s feature-absence markers do NOT include 'variable has incomplete type', so nothing in the tooling demotes a release that predates the construct. That is why control-struct-first.hlsl is run on EVERY probed release: it is byte-identical to repro.hlsl apart from an unreferenced 'struct Resources { SamplerState Samplers[2]; };' declaration, which the issue body says makes the error disappear. A release where the control also fails did not support sampler-array parameters in any form and is not evidence about this defect, whatever its diagnostic says. Negative control: control-no-sampler-array.hlsl (a single sampler passed by value) must score no-match.
